2	status: Accepted
3	date: 2026-11-20
4	decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
5	consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, MDN Web Docs (Window.sessionStorage)
6	informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
7	---
8	
9	# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
14	not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
15	US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
16	story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
17	where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
18	(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
19	US-01-Q-02, default accepted).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
24	- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
25	- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
26	- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
27	- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
28	- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
29	- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.
30	
31	## Considered Options
32	
33	1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
34	2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
35	   tab close and successful payment.
36	3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
37	4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
38	   memory only.
39	
40	## Decision Outcome
41	
42	Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
43	the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
44	partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
45	(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
46	clearing rules below (D4).
47	
48	### What is decided
49	
50	**Store and storage key**
51	
52	- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
53	  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
54	- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
55	  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
56	  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
57	  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
58	  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
59	  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
60	  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
61	  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
62	  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
63	- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
64	  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
65	  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
66	  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
67	- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
68	  lives only in the payment component's memory.
69	- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.
70	
71	**When it is written**
72	
73	- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
74	  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
75	  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
76	  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.
77	
78	**When it is read**
79	
80	- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
81	  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
82	  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
83	- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
84	  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
85	  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.
86	
87	**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**
88	
89	- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
90	  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
91	  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
92	- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
93	  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
94	  independent state.
95	
96	**When it is cleared**
97	
98	| Event | Effect | Owner |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
101	| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
102	| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
103	| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
104	| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |
105	
106	**Privacy rules**
107	
108	- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
109	  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
110	- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
111	  is never stored separately.
112	- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
113	  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
114	  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
115	- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
116	  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.
117	
118	### Consequences
119	
120	- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
121	  after a rejected payment (D6).
122	- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
123	- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
124	  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
125	- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
126	  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
127	  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
128	  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
129	- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
130	  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
131	  the data stays on the same device and profile.
132	- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
133	  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
134	  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
135	- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
136	  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
137	- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
138	  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.
139	
140	### Strongest argument against
141	
142	The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
143	tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
144	"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
145	session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
146	personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.
147	
148	**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
149	fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
150	back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
151	logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
152	device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
153	
154	### Confirmation
155	
156	- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
157	  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
158	  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
159	  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
160	  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
161	  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
162	  memory fallback.
163	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
164	  request).
165	- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
166	  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
167	  successful payment and not on a rejected one.
168	
169	## Pros and Cons of the Options
170	
171	### 1. In memory only
172	
173	- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
174	- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
175	- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
176	  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
177	- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
178	  guard.
179	
180	### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)
181	
182	- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
183	- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
184	- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
185	- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.
186	
187	### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry
188	
189	- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
190	- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
191	  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
192	- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
193	  overwrite each other's state.
194	
195	### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)
196	
197	- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
198	- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
199	  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
200	  some fields.
201	- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
202	  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.
203	
204	## More Information
205	
206	- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
207	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
208	  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
209	  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
210	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
211	  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
212	  hydrated from the store).
213	- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
214	  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
215	  required).
216	- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
217	  only on a valid Continuar.
218

### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)

Two shapes exist (ADR-0003, HC2 decision). Only the second one is consumed by US-02 and US-03.

**Stored editing values** (written on every change; what a reload restores):

- `country`: the country code of the context (see below).
- `values`: a map from field `key` to the **raw editing value**, as typed: a string for `text`,
  `number`, `select` and `date`, a boolean for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field.
  In-progress invalid values (for example `'2015.5'`) are stored as typed. A `number` or `date`
  input whose text the browser cannot read (`validity.badInput`; for example `1e`, or a partly
  cleared date) is stored as `''` in the wizard state and `sessionStorage` (AC-09, AC-21), while
  the typed text stays visible and the field is invalid through the Signal Forms parse error.
  Neither the form model nor the stored values ever hold `null` (ADR-0004).

**Typed step 1 output** (produced only on a valid "Continuar"; never on an invalid one):

- `country`: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) that matches a published
  `country` entry loaded from Strapi in this page load (ADR-0001). `CO` and `CL` are the seeded
  values; the type is not a fixed union of them.
- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. An empty **optional** `text`,
  `number`, `select` or `date` field → `null`. A `number` or `date` input, required or optional,
  whose text the browser cannot read is invalid, so no typed output is produced while it holds
  that text (v0.5, US-01-R3-F01, AC-09); it is never mapped to `null`. `checkbox` → always a boolean: checked → `true`,
  unchecked → `false`, also when the checkbox is optional (HC2 decision); a checkbox is never
  `null`.
- The field configuration is **not** stored: later steps read labels and option labels from the
  configuration fetched in the same page load (refetched on every full page load, ADR-0003,
  US-01-Q-16).
- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.

A `number` or `date` input whose text the browser cannot read (`validity.badInput`; for example `1e` in a number, or a partly cleared date) is not an empty optional field: it is invalid whether it is required or optional (v0.5, US-01-R3-F01; AC-09). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-02, US-01-AC-08, US-01-AC-09, US-01-AC-10, US-01-AC-14, US-01-AC-16 |

On 2026-11-20 the valid range is 2006–2027. The limits 20 and 1 are parameters of the `yearRange` rule in the configuration (seeded as 20 and 1 for both countries), so the business can change them (US-01-Q-05). | US-01-AC-05 |
112	| US-01-BR-04 | Story: "The policyholder must be of legal age." | The birth date is valid if and only if the age in completed years on *today* is ≥ the configured `minAge` (seeded as 18 for CO and for CL). A person turns N on the anniversary of their birth date; for a 29 February birth date, in non-leap years the anniversary is 1 March (US-01-Q-07). Birth dates after today are invalid. | US-01-AC-06 |
113	| US-01-BR-05 | Story context: "In Colombia the identity document is usually the citizenship ID (cédula de ciudadanía) or foreigner ID (cédula de extranjería), and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (placa). In Chile the document is the RUT and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (patente)." | CO step 1 includes a document type select with options CC "Cédula de ciudadanía" and CE "Cédula de extranjería", a document number (digits only, 6–10) and a plate labelled "Placa" (3 letters + 3 digits). CL step 1 includes a document number labelled "RUT" (with or without dots and dash, check digit `0–9`/`K`, check digit verified per US-01-Q-09) and a plate labelled "Patente" (2 letters + 4 digits, or 4 letters + 2 digits). CL has no document type field. These are **seed content**, not code; the seed is summarised in §7.2 and listed in full in the annex [seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md) (US-01-Q-03). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-11, US-01-AC-12 |
114	| US-01-BR-06 | Story context: "The business team wants to add, remove or reorder fields from Strapi without asking development for changes." Assessment: "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code." | Publishing, unpublishing or editing a field configuration (including its order, options, rules and copy) is reflected in step 1 on the next full page load of the app, with no code change, build or deployment. No browser-side or proxy cache may delay this beyond that reload (US-01-Q-16). Unpublished (draft) changes are never shown, and no anonymous caller (glossary: any request Strapi does not authenticate, whatever its headers or path letter case) can read them, not even by asking the content API for `status=draft` (ADR-0002). | US-01-AC-03, US-01-AC-13, US-01-AC-23, US-01-AC-28 |
115	| US-01-BR-07 | Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." Business context: "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy, so the content the app consumes changes by country." | One production build serves both countries. The supported countries are the published `country` entries in Strapi, loaded once per full page load (ADR-0001); no country code, country name or country list exists in front-end code. The country context selects which content is loaded; no country-specific branch, field list or copy exists in front-end code (wizard chrome copy excepted, US-01-Q-14; the complete list is §8.1). A country code that is not in the loaded list shows the unknown-country state and loads no form. If the country list cannot be loaded, the root chooser and the unknown-country page show a load error with "Reintentar", never "Este país no está disponible." (ADR-0001). Data entered in one country context is never shown in the other (US-01-Q-02). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-17, US-01-AC-22 |
116	| US-01-BR-08 | Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." Story AC "Keep data when going back". | Step 1 values stay in the browser: they are held in the wizard state on the front end and never sent to Strapi or any other server. They survive moving between steps (in-app and browser navigation) and a reload in the same tab; they are kept in `sessionStorage` for one country and cleared when the tab closes, when another country's context is entered and after a successful payment (ADR-0003). The store keeps the raw editing values and writes them on every change, so a reload restores exactly what was typed, valid or not (ADR-0003, HC2). Step 1 hands its values to the next steps only through the wizard state, as the typed output of §7.3, which is produced only on a valid "Continuar". | US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-18, US-01-AC-20, US-01-AC-21, US-01-AC-27 |

These are **seed content**, not code; the seed is summarised in §7.2 and listed in full in the annex [seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md) (US-01-Q-03). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-11, US-01-AC-12 |
114	| US-01-BR-06 | Story context: "The business team wants to add, remove or reorder fields from Strapi without asking development for changes." Assessment: "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code." | Publishing, unpublishing or editing a field configuration (including its order, options, rules and copy) is reflected in step 1 on the next full page load of the app, with no code change, build or deployment. No browser-side or proxy cache may delay this beyond that reload (US-01-Q-16). Unpublished (draft) changes are never shown, and no anonymous caller (glossary: any request Strapi does not authenticate, whatever its headers or path letter case) can read them, not even by asking the content API for `status=draft` (ADR-0002). | US-01-AC-03, US-01-AC-13, US-01-AC-23, US-01-AC-28 |
115	| US-01-BR-07 | Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." Business context: "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy, so the content the app consumes changes by country." | One production build serves both countries. The supported countries are the published `country` entries in Strapi, loaded once per full page load (ADR-0001); no country code, country name or country list exists in front-end code. The country context selects which content is loaded; no country-specific branch, field list or copy exists in front-end code (wizard chrome copy excepted, US-01-Q-14; the complete list is §8.1). A country code that is not in the loaded list shows the unknown-country state and loads no form. If the country list cannot be loaded, the root chooser and the unknown-country page show a load error with "Reintentar", never "Este país no está disponible." (ADR-0001). Data entered in one country context is never shown in the other (US-01-Q-02). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-17, US-01-AC-22 |
116	| US-01-BR-08 | Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." Story AC "Keep data when going back". | Step 1 values stay in the browser: they are held in the wizard state on the front end and never sent to Strapi or any other server. They survive moving between steps (in-app and browser navigation) and a reload in the same tab; they are kept in `sessionStorage` for one country and cleared when the tab closes, when another country's context is entered and after a successful payment (ADR-0003). The store keeps the raw editing values and writes them on every change, so a reload restores exactly what was typed, valid or not (ADR-0003, HC2). Step 1 hands its values to the next steps only through the wizard state, as the typed output of §7.3, which is produced only on a valid "Continuar". | US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-18, US-01-AC-20, US-01-AC-21, US-01-AC-27 |

---
status: Proposed
date: 2026-11-21
decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (approval), architect subagent (proposal)
consulted: specs/US-02/spec.md v0.1 (Approved; §6 US-02-Q-01, §7.6, §10), specs/US-02/seed-plans.md, specs/US-01/spec.md v0.5 §7.3 and US-01-BR-04, ADR-0001..0006, installed packages @strapi/core, @strapi/utils, @strapi/database 5.63.0 and @angular/router, @angular/core 22.3.0 (versions read from each package.json under backend/ and frontend/node_modules), Strapi REST docs (populate), MDN (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)
informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence; spec-writer (spec impact below); US-03 (reuses the rule)
---

# ADR-0007: Simulated price rule: formula in code, factor tables per country in Strapi

## Context and Problem Statement

Step 2 shows each plan's **final price**: its base price adjusted by "a simulated rule based on
the step 1 data. The rule is documented." (US-02 story, US-02-BR-04). The summary of US-03 must
show the same price. Spec §7.6 proposes a starting rule (a driver-age factor and a vehicle-age
factor, integer arithmetic, round half up, neutral factor with a warning when an input is
missing). At HC1 the human answered US-02-Q-01: "decided by an ADR that weighs **real
alternatives** (for example, factors configurable in Strapi); the proposed rule is the starting
point" (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21). We must decide where the rule's formula and its numbers live,
where it runs, how it rounds, which "today" it uses, how bad content is handled, and how US-03
reuses it. Story: US-02 (`specs/US-02/spec.md` §4 BR-04, §5 AC-07, §7.6); consumer: US-03.

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "Price calculation may be simulated: a real rating engine is not expected." and the rule
  "is documented" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-04). Simplicity is allowed; documentation is
  required.
- D2. "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the
  offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment."; evaluated as "form and plans 100%
  configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-06).
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app"; "Each country has its own
  regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment; ADR-0001 D3,
  D4).
- D4. Step 1 values never leave the browser (source: ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04,
  US-02-AC-19). The rule runs in the front end.
- D5. Public permissions minimal and justified; published content only; no write token in the
  browser (source: Assessment, security; ADR-0002 as amended by ADR-0005).
- D6. Keep bespoke backend code to a minimum (source: human decision recorded as D3 in ADR-0005 and
  D4 in ADR-0006).
- D7. Deterministic, exact prices in whole units: COP and CLP have no decimals; the result is an
  integer ≥ 1 (source: US-02-BR-03, US-02-BR-04, US-02-Q-06, US-02-Q-07).
- D8. "Today" comes from the injectable clock of US-01-Q-06, so tests pin it (source: US-01 spec
  glossary; `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `CLOCK`).
- D9. Malformed content is dropped at the boundary with a warning that names keys, never values,
  and the page keeps working (source: US-01-Q-18, US-02-Q-18, CLAUDE.md §3).
- D10. US-03 shows the same final price the person chose (source: spec §7.4 "For US-03").
- D11. Do not destabilise US-01, which is Ready for QA (source: `specs/US-01/tasks.md`).

## Considered Options

1. **A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function**: the §7.6 formula *and* its factors are
   constants in `price-rules.ts`, the same for both countries.
2. **B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`**: the formula stays in a pure
   front-end function; the two factor tables (driver age, vehicle age) are repeatable components
   on the existing `country` content type, edited in Strapi.
3. **C. Factor tables in a separate `pricing-rule` collection type** with a required `country`
   relation, its own draft & publish, router, permission and proxy path.
4. **D. Factor tables per plan**: the same two repeatable components on each `plan`, so each plan
   has its own sensitivity to age and vehicle age (a constant per-plan multiplier is discussed
   under this option).
5. **E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional per-country overrides in Strapi**: option A's
   constants apply unless the country entry carries tables.

Not considered further, because they contradict an accepted ADR: computing the price in a custom
Strapi endpoint that receives `birthDate` and `vehicleYear` (sends step 1 values to a server:
ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04); a free JSON or expression attribute holding the rule (ADR-0006
and the `strapi-content-modeling` skill forbid free JSON for editor-facing configuration).

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`"**, because it is the
only option that makes the numbers of the rule content, differentiated by country (D2, D3), with
**no new public permission, router, proxy path or backend code** (D5, D6): `country` is already
publicly readable through `find`, already routed with `publishedOnlyConfig()`, and already on the
proxy allow-list. The formula, rounding and fallbacks stay in one documented pure function (D1,
D7), which runs in the browser (D4) and is reused as is by US-03 (D10). The seed carries exactly
the §7.6 factors, so the documented starting rule is what runs on a fresh stack.

### What is decided

**Formula (code, `frontend/src/app/shared/price-rules.ts`, pure, no Angular dependency)**

```
calculateFinalPrice(basePrice, step1Output, pricing, today) →
  driverAge     = completed years between step1Output.values.birthDate and today
                  (same reckoning as US-01-BR-04: 29 Feb birthdays turn on 1 Mar in non-leap years)
  vehicleAge    = max(0, year(today) − step1Output.values.vehicleYear)
  driverPct     = factorPercent of the driver-age band containing driverAge, else 100
  vehiclePct    = factorPercent of the vehicle-age band containing vehicleAge, else 100
  final         = max(1, floor((basePrice × driverPct × vehiclePct + 5000) / 10000))
```

- **Integer arithmetic.** Factors are integer **percentages** (`120` means ×1.20, `100` is
  neutral). `basePrice ≤ 2 147 483 647` (US-02-BR-01) and `factorPercent ≤ 1000` (schema below)
  bound the numerator to about 2.15 × 10¹⁵, below `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`
  (9 007 199 254 740 991; MDN: "'Safe' in this context refers to the ability to represent integers
  exactly and to compare them correctly"), so every step is exact in a JavaScript `number`. No
  floating-point factor is ever multiplied.
- **Rounding.** `floor((n + 5000) / 10000)` is round half up for the positive integers involved
  (49.5 → 50, 59.4 → 59; US-02-AC-07). The result is in whole units of the country's currency; it
  is never rounded to a currency-specific step (COP and CLP have no decimals, US-02-Q-07).
  Formatting stays `Intl.NumberFormat` with no fraction digits (US-02-BR-03).
- **Clock.** `today` is a parameter. Callers pass the value of the `CLOCK` injection token
  (`frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `InjectionToken<() => Date>`, US-01-Q-06). Tests pin it.
- **Missing inputs.** `birthDate` or `vehicleYear` absent from the typed step 1 output (an editor
  removed the reserved field) or `null` (an empty optional field) → that factor is `100` and a
  `console.warn` names the key (`birthDate`, `vehicleYear`), never the value (US-02-BR-04,
  US-01-Q-08).
- **No band matches** (a gap in the table, or an empty or absent table) → that factor is `100` and
  a `console.warn` names the table (`driverAgeFactors`, `vehicleAgeFactors`) and the country code,
  never the age.
- The function is synchronous and has no side effects other than the warnings.

**Numbers (content, Strapi)**

- New component **`pricing.age-band`** (`backend/src/components/pricing/age-band.json`):

  | Attribute | Strapi type | Rules |
  |---|---|---|
  | `fromYears` | integer, required, `min: 0` | Inclusive lower bound, in completed years. |
  | `toYears` | integer, optional, `min: 0` | Inclusive upper bound; empty means "and older". |
  | `factorPercent` | integer, required, `min: 1`, `max: 1000` | `100` = no adjustment; `120` = +20 %; `90` = −10 %. |

  Admin descriptions are in Spanish and state the meaning of `100`, and that bands must not
  overlap.
- `country` gains two attributes (allowed by ADR-0001: "Later stories may add country-level
  attributes … through their own spec"): **`driverAgeFactors`** and **`vehicleAgeFactors`**,
  each a repeatable `pricing.age-band`, not required (an empty table means "no adjustment").
- Seed: both countries get the §7.6 values: driver `18–25 → 120`, `26–60 → 100`, `61– → 110`;
  vehicle `0–5 → 110`, `6–10 → 100`, `11– → 90`. Countries are seeded with the tables when they are
  created. The seed stays create-only (it never overwrites editor changes), so an existing
  development database must have its Strapi volume reset once, as for ADR-0006.

**Loading and boundary validation (front end)**

- Step 2 loads the tables of its country in **one request, separate from the US-01 country
  list**, through the existing proxy path:
  `GET /api/countries?filters[code][$eq]=CO&fields[0]=code`
  `&populate[driverAgeFactors][fields][0]=fromYears&populate[driverAgeFactors][fields][1]=toYears&populate[driverAgeFactors][fields][2]=factorPercent`
  `&populate[vehicleAgeFactors][fields][0]=fromYears&…` (built with the existing
  `content-request.ts` helper, not hand-concatenated). It runs in parallel with the plans
  request, under the same 10 s timeout, once per full page load (held in memory, like the plans;
  never stored, ADR-0003). The US-01 country-list request and its parser are **not changed**
  (D11).
- If the request fails or times out, step 2 shows its existing error state with "Reintentar"
  (prices cannot be computed). If it succeeds, bad content never blocks the page:
  - A band is dropped with a warning (country code, table name, band position) when `fromYears`
    is not an integer ≥ 0, `toYears` is neither `null` nor an integer ≥ `fromYears`, or
    `factorPercent` is not an integer in 1..1000.
  - The kept bands are sorted by `fromYears`; a band that overlaps an earlier kept band is
    dropped with a warning (the "first in order wins" rule of US-02-Q-09 and duplicate plan keys).
  - A table that is absent, `null`, not an array, or empty after dropping → every lookup in it is
    neutral (`100`), with one warning.
- The parser lives in `frontend/src/app/shared/` next to the other boundary parsers; exact file
  and type names are set by the spec (CLAUDE.md §6: `pricing.ts`, `pricing.model.ts` are the
  expected names).

**Security**

- No new public permission: `api::country.country.find` already exists (ADR-0002) and covers the
  components. Strapi checks read permissions on **relations** used in `populate`/`filters`, not on
  components (verified below), so `populate[driverAgeFactors]` needs nothing else.
- Published only: the `country` router already uses `publishedOnlyConfig()`
  (`backend/src/api/country/routes/country.ts`), so drafts of the tables are never readable
  anonymously; `backend/tests/published-only-routes.test.ts` already covers `country`.
- The request carries only the country code, so no step 1 value is sent (US-02-AC-19). The
  factors are public by nature: they describe a documented, simulated rule.
- No e2e test writes to `country`, so ADR-0005's token scope does not change.

**Reuse by US-03**

US-03 imports the same `calculateFinalPrice`, the same pricing parser and loader, the typed step 1
output (re-derived as in US-02-Q-17) and the same `CLOCK`. The summary therefore shows the price
step 2 showed, unless "today" or published content changed between the two computations (a
birthday at midnight, or an editor publishing new factors before a reload); that is the intended
behaviour of a recomputed, never-stored price (ADR-0003, US-02-BR-06).

### Consequences

- Good, because the business can change the price adjustment per country, without a deployment,
  by editing and publishing the country entry (D2, D3).
- Good, because the documented starting rule is what runs: the seed equals §7.6, and every
  US-02-AC-07 Example keeps its value.
- Good, because the change adds no permission, router, proxy rule, middleware or controller
  (D5, D6); the Strapi side is one component file, two attributes and seed data.
- Good, because formula, rounding and fallbacks are one pure, exhaustively unit-testable function
  that US-03 reuses (D7, D10).
- Bad, because an editor can publish tables that Strapi cannot reject: overlapping bands, gaps,
  or `toYears < fromYears` (Strapi validates each attribute's type and `min`/`max`, never relations
  between items of a repeatable component) — mitigation: the boundary rules above, warnings in the
  console, a Spanish admin description, and the HC3 check below. The failure is a neutral price,
  never a broken page.
- Bad, because `min` on integers and on repeatable components is not enforced for drafts (verified
  below), so a draft can hold out-of-range values — mitigation: only published content is read,
  and the boundary parser re-checks every value.
- Bad, because pricing now shares the `country` entry with US-01's code, name, currency and
  locale: editing factors means opening and republishing the country — mitigation: the country
  list request and parser of US-01 are untouched; republishing with unchanged US-01 attributes has
  no effect on step 1.
- Bad, because step 2 now depends on two requests, and the pricing request can fail on its own —
  mitigation: both run in parallel with the same timeout, and either failure leads to the same
  error state and "Reintentar" (spec impact 4).
- Bad, because the create-only seed cannot add the tables to an existing development database —
  mitigation: reset the Strapi volume once (stated in the commit and README), as for ADR-0006.
- Neutral: the formula is the same for every country; only the numbers differ. A country that
  needs another kind of input (for example the city) needs a new ADR or spec revision.

### Strongest argument against

Option A does everything the assessment asks for, at a fraction of the cost. The assessment says
the price "may be simulated" and "a real rating engine is not expected"; the story says the rule
must be **documented**. A fixed function documented in this ADR meets both completely, cannot be
misconfigured, needs no schema change on a content type US-01 already depends on, no second
request with its own failure mode, no band parser with overlap and gap semantics, and no seed
volume reset. Option B turns a fake rating engine into a configurable one that nobody asked to
configure, and it weakens "the rule is documented": the documented numbers are only the seed, and
the numbers that actually run are whatever an editor last published. Worse, a misconfigured band
fails **quietly**: the price falls back to a neutral, plausible-looking amount, visible only as a
console warning that a business user will never read.

**Why we accept it:** the human asked at HC1 for a rule weighed against "factors configurable in
Strapi", and the evaluation criterion is "form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi", with
content "differentiated by country". Under option A, the price a Colombian or Chilean visitor sees
depends on numbers only a developer can change, the same in both countries. Option B keeps the
part that must be documented (the formula, rounding, fallbacks) in code and in this ADR, and
makes only the numbers content, at the cost of one component and two attributes, with no new
backend code or permission. The quiet-failure risk is bounded: bands are validated at the
boundary, the HC3 manual check covers an edit in the admin, and the revisit condition below
reopens the decision if editors misconfigure tables in practice.

### Confirmation

- Unit tests `price-rules.spec.ts` (clock pinned to 2026-11-21, the seed tables as a fixture): every
  US-02-AC-07 row; integer exactness at the bounds (`basePrice` 2 147 483 647 with factors 1000 and
  1000 gives an exact result); result ≥ 1; missing and `null` inputs warn with the key and without
  the value; a gap and an empty table give a neutral factor with a warning.
- Unit tests for the pricing parser: every dropped-band case above, overlap resolution, absent and
  non-array tables.
- E2E (`full-flow-co`, `plans-cl-content`): the seed prices of US-02-AC-07 with the browser clock
  pinned; US-02-AC-19 network inspection shows the pricing request is a `GET` without
  `Authorization` and without step 1 values.
- Review checklist: no factor, band or percentage literal in `frontend/src` outside tests and
  fixtures; `price-rules.ts` has no Angular import and no `new Date()`; the country router still
  uses `publishedOnlyConfig()`; bootstrap's public role list is unchanged by this ADR.
- HC3 manual check: in the Strapi admin, change one CL `factorPercent`, publish, reload step 2 of
  Chile, see the new price; restore it.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function

`price-rules.ts` holds both the formula and the §7.6 factors; US-03 imports it.

- Good, because it is the smallest change: one pure function, no schema, seed, request or parser.
- Good, because nothing can be misconfigured, and the documented rule is exactly the running rule
  (D1).
- Good, because it has no new failure mode on step 2.
- Bad, because changing a factor needs a code change and a deployment (against D2).
- Bad, because both countries get the same adjustment; differentiating them would need a
  per-country branch in code, which US-01-BR-07 and ADR-0001 forbid (against D3).

### B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country` (chosen)

- Good, because the numbers are content per country, editable without a deployment (D2, D3).
- Good, because it reuses the country's existing public `find`, router and proxy path (D5, D6).
- Good, because the formula stays a documented pure function (D1, D7).
- Bad, because Strapi cannot validate band consistency; the front end must (D9).
- Bad, because the tables share draft & publish and editing with the country entry.
- Bad, because step 2 makes a second request.

### C. Separate `pricing-rule` collection type

One document per country with a required `country` relation and the same two repeatable
components.

- Good, because pricing has its own draft & publish, history and admin entry, apart from the
  country's identity attributes.
- Good, because its permission could later differ from `country`'s.
- Bad, because it adds a public permission `api::pricing-rule.pricing-rule.find`, a router with
  `publishedOnlyConfig()`, a proxy allow-list entry, a bootstrap reconciliation change, and
  `country.find` for the relation filter (against D5, D6).
- Bad, because "exactly one rule per country" is not expressible in Strapi (`unique` is not
  scoped by relation, ADR-0001): it needs a Document Service middleware like the field-key one, or
  a front-end "first one wins" rule (against D6).

### D. Factor tables per plan

The two components on each `plan`, read in the plans request.

- Good, because one request carries plans and factors: no second request and no new failure
  mode.
- Good, because a plan can price risk differently (a young-driver plan with a gentler age factor).
- Bad, because editors must repeat and keep in step the same tables on every plan of every
  country (six tables per country with the seed); a forgotten plan prices differently with no
  visible error.
- Bad, because it is more than the story asks: the rule is "based on the step 1 data", not per
  plan.
- Variant, a **constant per-plan multiplier**: it does not use step 1 data, so it is equivalent
  to editing `basePrice` and adds nothing to the rule.

### E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional Strapi overrides

- Good, because a fresh or misconfigured country still gets the documented factors instead of a
  neutral price.
- Bad, because there are two sources of truth: an editor cannot tell from the admin which numbers
  apply, and emptying a table brings back hidden code values instead of "no adjustment".
- Bad, because pricing numbers stay in front-end code, against the content-only rule of
  US-02-BR-06.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

The approved spec v0.1 anticipated this case ("unless the ADR for US-02-Q-01 chooses that
option"; AC-07 "Examples are updated if the ADR decides otherwise"). If this ADR is accepted, the
spec needs a revision:

1. §2: "Price rule parameters edited in Strapi" moves from out of scope to in scope.
2. §7: the `country` contract gains `driverAgeFactors` and `vehicleAgeFactors`
   (`pricing.age-band`); §7.2 adds the pricing request; §7.3 and the annex add the seeded tables
   per country; §7.6 becomes the formula above plus the seeded tables (factors as percentages).
3. US-02-BR-04 and US-02-BR-06: the rule's numbers are content; the fallbacks add "no matching
   band", "empty or absent table" and the dropped-band rules. AC-07's Examples keep their values;
   rows (or a new derived AC) cover dropped and overlapping bands, gaps and empty tables at unit
   level.
4. US-02-AC-11 and §8 "Error": the trigger includes the pricing request failing or timing out.
5. §9 Performance: two requests per step 2 load (plans and pricing), in parallel.
6. A derived AC (or an AC-12 row) for "a factor change is reflected without deployment",
   verified manually at HC3 (no e2e writes to `country`).
7. §11 and `tasks.md`: a parser test file, the strapi-developer task for the component, the two
   attributes and the seed, and the frontend task for the pricing loader.

## More Information

- Verified in the installed packages (versions from each `package.json`: `@strapi/core`,
  `@strapi/utils`, `@strapi/database`, `@strapi/strapi` 5.63.0 in `backend/node_modules`;
  `@angular/core`, `@angular/router` 22.3.0 in `frontend/node_modules`), on 2026-11-21:
  - Components need no read permission of their own: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
    `dist/validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` returns early unless
    `attribute.type === 'relation'`, and checks `<target>.find` only for relations.
  - A component can be populated with `fields`: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
    `dist/convert-query-params.js:367-385` resolves `attribute.type === 'component'` to the
    component schema and passes the sub-populate to `convertNestedPopulate`, which converts
    `fields` (lines 395-416).
  - Integer validation: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/validators.js:322-328`
    (`yup.number().integer()`); `min` is skipped for drafts (lines 75-78), `max` always applies
    (lines 81-84).
  - Repeatable components: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/index.js:35-44`
    and `92-110`: `min`/`max` on the list apply only when not a draft, and `min` only when the
    attribute is required or the list is non-empty. There is no cross-item validation.
  - `integer` is read back as a JavaScript number: `@strapi/database@5.63.0`
    `dist/fields/index.js:25` maps `integer` to the number field.
  - `CLOCK` exists as `InjectionToken<() => Date>` in `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`.
- Strapi REST docs, "Populate and select" (https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/populate-select,
  read 2026-11-21): "The REST API by default does not populate any relations, media fields,
  components, or dynamic zones."
- MDN, `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Number/MAX_SAFE_INTEGER,
  read 2026-11-21): value 9 007 199 254 740 991.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country-level attributes live on `country`), ADR-0002 and ADR-0005
  (public `country.find`, published only, proxy; no change), ADR-0003 (prices never stored),
  ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON; `localeTag` for formatting).
- Revisit when: editors publish inconsistent tables more than occasionally (move to option C with
  a server-side consistency check, or to option A); a country needs a rule input other than age
  and vehicle age; plans need different sensitivities (option D); or a real rating engine replaces
  the simulation.

# ADR-0007: Simulated price rule: formula in code, factor tables per country in Strapi

## Context and Problem Statement

Step 2 shows each plan's **final price**: its base price adjusted by "a simulated rule based on
the step 1 data. The rule is documented." (US-02 story, US-02-BR-04). The summary of US-03 must
show the same price. Spec §7.6 proposes a starting rule (a driver-age factor and a vehicle-age
factor, integer arithmetic, round half up, neutral factor with a warning when an input is
missing). At HC1 the human answered US-02-Q-01: "decided by an ADR that weighs **real
alternatives** (for example, factors configurable in Strapi); the proposed rule is the starting
point" (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21). We must decide where the rule's formula and its numbers live,
where it runs, how it rounds, which "today" it uses, how bad content is handled, and how US-03
reuses it. Story: US-02 (`specs/US-02/spec.md` §4 BR-04, §5 AC-07, §7.6); consumer: US-03.

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "Price calculation may be simulated: a real rating engine is not expected." and the rule
  "is documented" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-04). Simplicity is allowed; documentation is
  required.
- D2. "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the
  offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment."; evaluated as "form and plans 100%
  configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-06).
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app"; "Each country has its own
  regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment; ADR-0001 D3,
  D4).
- D4. Step 1 values never leave the browser (source: ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04,
  US-02-AC-19). The rule runs in the front end.
- D5. Public permissions minimal and justified; published content only; no write token in the
  browser (source: Assessment, security; ADR-0002 as amended by ADR-0005).
- D6. Keep bespoke backend code to a minimum (source: human decision recorded as D3 in ADR-0005 and
  D4 in ADR-0006).
- D7. Deterministic, exact prices in whole units: COP and CLP have no decimals; the result is an
  integer ≥ 1 (source: US-02-BR-03, US-02-BR-04, US-02-Q-06, US-02-Q-07).
- D8. "Today" comes from the injectable clock of US-01-Q-06, so tests pin it (source: US-01 spec
  glossary; `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `CLOCK`).
- D9. Malformed content is dropped at the boundary with a warning that names keys, never values,
  and the page keeps working (source: US-01-Q-18, US-02-Q-18, CLAUDE.md §3).
- D10. US-03 shows the same final price the person chose (source: spec §7.4 "For US-03").
- D11. Do not destabilise US-01, which is Ready for QA (source: `specs/US-01/tasks.md`).

## Considered Options

1. **A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function**: the §7.6 formula *and* its factors are
   constants in `price-rules.ts`, the same for both countries.
2. **B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`**: the formula stays in a pure
   front-end function; the two factor tables (driver age, vehicle age) are repeatable components
   on the existing `country` content type, edited in Strapi.
3. **C. Factor tables in a separate `pricing-rule` collection type** with a required `country`
   relation, its own draft & publish, router, permission and proxy path.
4. **D. Factor tables per plan**: the same two repeatable components on each `plan`, so each plan
   has its own sensitivity to age and vehicle age (a constant per-plan multiplier is discussed
   under this option).
5. **E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional per-country overrides in Strapi**: option A's
   constants apply unless the country entry carries tables.

Not considered further, because they contradict an accepted ADR: computing the price in a custom
Strapi endpoint that receives `birthDate` and `vehicleYear` (sends step 1 values to a server:
ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04); a free JSON or expression attribute holding the rule (ADR-0006
and the `strapi-content-modeling` skill forbid free JSON for editor-facing configuration).

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`"**, because it is the
only option that makes the numbers of the rule content, differentiated by country (D2, D3), with
**no new public permission, router, proxy path or backend code** (D5, D6): `country` is already
publicly readable through `find`, already routed with `publishedOnlyConfig()`, and already on the
proxy allow-list. The formula, rounding and fallbacks stay in one documented pure function (D1,
D7), which runs in the browser (D4) and is reused as is by US-03 (D10). The seed carries exactly
the §7.6 factors, so the documented starting rule is what runs on a fresh stack.

### What is decided

**Formula (code, `frontend/src/app/shared/price-rules.ts`, pure, no Angular dependency)**

```
calculateFinalPrice(basePrice, step1Output, pricing, today) →
  driverAge     = completed years between step1Output.values.birthDate and today
                  (same reckoning as US-01-BR-04: 29 Feb birthdays turn on 1 Mar in non-leap years)
  vehicleAge    = max(0, year(today) − step1Output.values.vehicleYear)
  driverPct     = factorPercent of the driver-age band containing driverAge, else 100
  vehiclePct    = factorPercent of the vehicle-age band containing vehicleAge, else 100
  final         = max(1, floor((basePrice × driverPct × vehiclePct + 5000) / 10000))
```

- **Integer arithmetic.** Factors are integer **percentages** (`120` means ×1.20, `100` is
  neutral). `basePrice ≤ 2 147 483 647` (US-02-BR-01) and `factorPercent ≤ 1000` (schema below)
  bound the numerator to about 2.15 × 10¹⁵, below `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`
  (9 007 199 254 740 991; MDN: "'Safe' in this context refers to the ability to represent integers
  exactly and to compare them correctly"), so every step is exact in a JavaScript `number`. No
  floating-point factor is ever multiplied.
- **Rounding.** `floor((n + 5000) / 10000)` is round half up for the positive integers involved
  (49.5 → 50, 59.4 → 59; US-02-AC-07). The result is in whole units of the country's currency; it
  is never rounded to a currency-specific step (COP and CLP have no decimals, US-02-Q-07).
  Formatting stays `Intl.NumberFormat` with no fraction digits (US-02-BR-03).
- **Clock.** `today` is a parameter. Callers pass the value of the `CLOCK` injection token
  (`frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `InjectionToken<() => Date>`, US-01-Q-06). Tests pin it.
- **Missing inputs.** `birthDate` or `vehicleYear` absent from the typed step 1 output (an editor
  removed the reserved field) or `null` (an empty optional field) → that factor is `100` and a
  `console.warn` names the key (`birthDate`, `vehicleYear`), never the value (US-02-BR-04,
  US-01-Q-08).
- **No band matches** (a gap in the table, or an empty or absent table) → that factor is `100` and
  a `console.warn` names the table (`driverAgeFactors`, `vehicleAgeFactors`) and the country code,
  never the age.
- The function is synchronous and has no side effects other than the warnings.

**Numbers (content, Strapi)**

- New component **`pricing.age-band`** (`backend/src/components/pricing/age-band.json`):

  | Attribute | Strapi type | Rules |
  |---|---|---|
  | `fromYears` | integer, required, `min: 0` | Inclusive lower bound, in completed years. |
  | `toYears` | integer, optional, `min: 0` | Inclusive upper bound; empty means "and older". |
  | `factorPercent` | integer, required, `min: 1`, `max: 1000` | `100` = no adjustment; `120` = +20 %; `90` = −10 %. |

  Admin descriptions are in Spanish and state the meaning of `100`, and that bands must not
  overlap.
- `country` gains two attributes (allowed by ADR-0001: "Later stories may add country-level
  attributes … through their own spec"): **`driverAgeFactors`** and **`vehicleAgeFactors`**,
  each a repeatable `pricing.age-band`, not required (an empty table means "no adjustment").
- Seed: both countries get the §7.6 values: driver `18–25 → 120`, `26–60 → 100`, `61– → 110`;
  vehicle `0–5 → 110`, `6–10 → 100`, `11– → 90`. Countries are seeded with the tables when they are
  created. The seed stays create-only (it never overwrites editor changes), so an existing
  development database must have its Strapi volume reset once, as for ADR-0006.

**Loading and boundary validation (front end)**

- Step 2 loads the tables of its country in **one request, separate from the US-01 country
  list**, through the existing proxy path:
  `GET /api/countries?filters[code][$eq]=CO&fields[0]=code`
  `&populate[driverAgeFactors][fields][0]=fromYears&populate[driverAgeFactors][fields][1]=toYears&populate[driverAgeFactors][fields][2]=factorPercent`
  `&populate[vehicleAgeFactors][fields][0]=fromYears&…` (built with the existing
  `content-request.ts` helper, not hand-concatenated). It runs in parallel with the plans
  request, under the same 10 s timeout, once per full page load (held in memory, like the plans;
  never stored, ADR-0003). The US-01 country-list request and its parser are **not changed**
  (D11).
- If the request fails or times out, step 2 shows its existing error state with "Reintentar"
  (prices cannot be computed). If it succeeds, bad content never blocks the page:
  - A band is dropped with a warning (country code, table name, band position) when `fromYears`
    is not an integer ≥ 0, `toYears` is neither `null` nor an integer ≥ `fromYears`, or
    `factorPercent` is not an integer in 1..1000.
  - The kept bands are sorted by `fromYears`; a band that overlaps an earlier kept band is
    dropped with a warning (the "first in order wins" rule of US-02-Q-09 and duplicate plan keys).
  - A table that is absent, `null`, not an array, or empty after dropping → every lookup in it is
    neutral (`100`), with one warning.
- The parser lives in `frontend/src/app/shared/` next to the other boundary parsers; exact file
  and type names are set by the spec (CLAUDE.md §6: `pricing.ts`, `pricing.model.ts` are the
  expected names).

**Security**

- No new public permission: `api::country.country.find` already exists (ADR-0002) and covers the
  components. Strapi checks read permissions on **relations** used in `populate`/`filters`, not on
  components (verified below), so `populate[driverAgeFactors]` needs nothing else.
- Published only: the `country` router already uses `publishedOnlyConfig()`
  (`backend/src/api/country/routes/country.ts`), so drafts of the tables are never readable
  anonymously; `backend/tests/published-only-routes.test.ts` already covers `country`.
- The request carries only the country code, so no step 1 value is sent (US-02-AC-19). The
  factors are public by nature: they describe a documented, simulated rule.
- No e2e test writes to `country`, so ADR-0005's token scope does not change.

**Reuse by US-03**

US-03 imports the same `calculateFinalPrice`, the same pricing parser and loader, the typed step 1
output (re-derived as in US-02-Q-17) and the same `CLOCK`. The summary therefore shows the price
step 2 showed, unless "today" or published content changed between the two computations (a
birthday at midnight, or an editor publishing new factors before a reload); that is the intended
behaviour of a recomputed, never-stored price (ADR-0003, US-02-BR-06).

### Consequences

- Good, because the business can change the price adjustment per country, without a deployment,
  by editing and publishing the country entry (D2, D3).
- Good, because the documented starting rule is what runs: the seed equals §7.6, and every
  US-02-AC-07 Example keeps its value.
- Good, because the change adds no permission, router, proxy rule, middleware or controller
  (D5, D6); the Strapi side is one component file, two attributes and seed data.
- Good, because formula, rounding and fallbacks are one pure, exhaustively unit-testable function
  that US-03 reuses (D7, D10).
- Bad, because an editor can publish tables that Strapi cannot reject: overlapping bands, gaps,
  or `toYears < fromYears` (Strapi validates each attribute's type and `min`/`max`, never relations
  between items of a repeatable component) — mitigation: the boundary rules above, warnings in the
  console, a Spanish admin description, and the HC3 check below. The failure is a neutral price,
  never a broken page.
- Bad, because `min` on integers and on repeatable components is not enforced for drafts (verified
  below), so a draft can hold out-of-range values — mitigation: only published content is read,
  and the boundary parser re-checks every value.
- Bad, because pricing now shares the `country` entry with US-01's code, name, currency and
  locale: editing factors means opening and republishing the country — mitigation: the country
  list request and parser of US-01 are untouched; republishing with unchanged US-01 attributes has
  no effect on step 1.
- Bad, because step 2 now depends on two requests, and the pricing request can fail on its own —
  mitigation: both run in parallel with the same timeout, and either failure leads to the same
  error state and "Reintentar" (spec impact 4).
- Bad, because the create-only seed cannot add the tables to an existing development database —
  mitigation: reset the Strapi volume once (stated in the commit and README), as for ADR-0006.
- Neutral: the formula is the same for every country; only the numbers differ. A country that
  needs another kind of input (for example the city) needs a new ADR or spec revision.

### Strongest argument against

Option A does everything the assessment asks for, at a fraction of the cost. The assessment says
the price "may be simulated" and "a real rating engine is not expected"; the story says the rule
must be **documented**. A fixed function documented in this ADR meets both completely, cannot be
misconfigured, needs no schema change on a content type US-01 already depends on, no second
request with its own failure mode, no band parser with overlap and gap semantics, and no seed
volume reset. Option B turns a fake rating engine into a configurable one that nobody asked to
configure, and it weakens "the rule is documented": the documented numbers are only the seed, and
the numbers that actually run are whatever an editor last published. Worse, a misconfigured band
fails **quietly**: the price falls back to a neutral, plausible-looking amount, visible only as a
console warning that a business user will never read.

**Why we accept it:** the human asked at HC1 for a rule weighed against "factors configurable in
Strapi", and the evaluation criterion is "form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi", with
content "differentiated by country". Under option A, the price a Colombian or Chilean visitor sees
depends on numbers only a developer can change, the same in both countries. Option B keeps the
part that must be documented (the formula, rounding, fallbacks) in code and in this ADR, and
makes only the numbers content, at the cost of one component and two attributes, with no new
backend code or permission. The quiet-failure risk is bounded: bands are validated at the
boundary, the HC3 manual check covers an edit in the admin, and the revisit condition below
reopens the decision if editors misconfigure tables in practice.

### Confirmation

- Unit tests `price-rules.spec.ts` (clock pinned to 2026-11-21, the seed tables as a fixture): every
  US-02-AC-07 row; integer exactness at the bounds (`basePrice` 2 147 483 647 with factors 1000 and
  1000 gives an exact result); result ≥ 1; missing and `null` inputs warn with the key and without
  the value; a gap and an empty table give a neutral factor with a warning.
- Unit tests for the pricing parser: every dropped-band case above, overlap resolution, absent and
  non-array tables.
- E2E (`full-flow-co`, `plans-cl-content`): the seed prices of US-02-AC-07 with the browser clock
  pinned; US-02-AC-19 network inspection shows the pricing request is a `GET` without
  `Authorization` and without step 1 values.
- Review checklist: no factor, band or percentage literal in `frontend/src` outside tests and
  fixtures; `price-rules.ts` has no Angular import and no `new Date()`; the country router still
  uses `publishedOnlyConfig()`; bootstrap's public role list is unchanged by this ADR.
- HC3 manual check: in the Strapi admin, change one CL `factorPercent`, publish, reload step 2 of
  Chile, see the new price; restore it.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function

`price-rules.ts` holds both the formula and the §7.6 factors; US-03 imports it.

- Good, because it is the smallest change: one pure function, no schema, seed, request or parser.
- Good, because nothing can be misconfigured, and the documented rule is exactly the running rule
  (D1).
- Good, because it has no new failure mode on step 2.
- Bad, because changing a factor needs a code change and a deployment (against D2).
- Bad, because both countries get the same adjustment; differentiating them would need a
  per-country branch in code, which US-01-BR-07 and ADR-0001 forbid (against D3).

### B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country` (chosen)

- Good, because the numbers are content per country, editable without a deployment (D2, D3).
- Good, because it reuses the country's existing public `find`, router and proxy path (D5, D6).
- Good, because the formula stays a documented pure function (D1, D7).
- Bad, because Strapi cannot validate band consistency; the front end must (D9).
- Bad, because the tables share draft & publish and editing with the country entry.
- Bad, because step 2 makes a second request.

### C. Separate `pricing-rule` collection type

One document per country with a required `country` relation and the same two repeatable
components.

- Good, because pricing has its own draft & publish, history and admin entry, apart from the
  country's identity attributes.
- Good, because its permission could later differ from `country`'s.
- Bad, because it adds a public permission `api::pricing-rule.pricing-rule.find`, a router with
  `publishedOnlyConfig()`, a proxy allow-list entry, a bootstrap reconciliation change, and
  `country.find` for the relation filter (against D5, D6).
- Bad, because "exactly one rule per country" is not expressible in Strapi (`unique` is not
  scoped by relation, ADR-0001): it needs a Document Service middleware like the field-key one, or
  a front-end "first one wins" rule (against D6).

### D. Factor tables per plan

The two components on each `plan`, read in the plans request.

- Good, because one request carries plans and factors: no second request and no new failure
  mode.
- Good, because a plan can price risk differently (a young-driver plan with a gentler age factor).
- Bad, because editors must repeat and keep in step the same tables on every plan of every
  country (six tables per country with the seed); a forgotten plan prices differently with no
  visible error.
- Bad, because it is more than the story asks: the rule is "based on the step 1 data", not per
  plan.
- Variant, a **constant per-plan multiplier**: it does not use step 1 data, so it is equivalent
  to editing `basePrice` and adds nothing to the rule.

### E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional Strapi overrides

- Good, because a fresh or misconfigured country still gets the documented factors instead of a
  neutral price.
- Bad, because there are two sources of truth: an editor cannot tell from the admin which numbers
  apply, and emptying a table brings back hidden code values instead of "no adjustment".
- Bad, because pricing numbers stay in front-end code, against the content-only rule of
  US-02-BR-06.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

The approved spec v0.1 anticipated this case ("unless the ADR for US-02-Q-01 chooses that
option"; AC-07 "Examples are updated if the ADR decides otherwise"). If this ADR is accepted, the
spec needs a revision:

1. §2: "Price rule parameters edited in Strapi" moves from out of scope to in scope.
2. §7: the `country` contract gains `driverAgeFactors` and `vehicleAgeFactors`
   (`pricing.age-band`); §7.2 adds the pricing request; §7.3 and the annex add the seeded tables
   per country; §7.6 becomes the formula above plus the seeded tables (factors as percentages).
3. US-02-BR-04 and US-02-BR-06: the rule's numbers are content; the fallbacks add "no matching
   band", "empty or absent table" and the dropped-band rules. AC-07's Examples keep their values;
   rows (or a new derived AC) cover dropped and overlapping bands, gaps and empty tables at unit
   level.
4. US-02-AC-11 and §8 "Error": the trigger includes the pricing request failing or timing out.
5. §9 Performance: two requests per step 2 load (plans and pricing), in parallel.
6. A derived AC (or an AC-12 row) for "a factor change is reflected without deployment",
   verified manually at HC3 (no e2e writes to `country`).
7. §11 and `tasks.md`: a parser test file, the strapi-developer task for the component, the two
   attributes and the seed, and the frontend task for the pricing loader.

## More Information

- Verified in the installed packages (versions from each `package.json`: `@strapi/core`,
  `@strapi/utils`, `@strapi/database`, `@strapi/strapi` 5.63.0 in `backend/node_modules`;
  `@angular/core`, `@angular/router` 22.3.0 in `frontend/node_modules`), on 2026-11-21:
  - Components need no read permission of their own: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
    `dist/validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` returns early unless
    `attribute.type === 'relation'`, and checks `<target>.find` only for relations.
  - A component can be populated with `fields`: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
    `dist/convert-query-params.js:367-385` resolves `attribute.type === 'component'` to the
    component schema and passes the sub-populate to `convertNestedPopulate`, which converts
    `fields` (lines 395-416).
  - Integer validation: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/validators.js:322-328`
    (`yup.number().integer()`); `min` is skipped for drafts (lines 75-78), `max` always applies
    (lines 81-84).
  - Repeatable components: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/index.js:35-44`
    and `92-110`: `min`/`max` on the list apply only when not a draft, and `min` only when the
    attribute is required or the list is non-empty. There is no cross-item validation.
  - `integer` is read back as a JavaScript number: `@strapi/database@5.63.0`
    `dist/fields/index.js:25` maps `integer` to the number field.
  - `CLOCK` exists as `InjectionToken<() => Date>` in `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`.
- Strapi REST docs, "Populate and select" (https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/populate-select,
  read 2026-11-21): "The REST API by default does not populate any relations, media fields,
  components, or dynamic zones."
- MDN, `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Number/MAX_SAFE_INTEGER,
  read 2026-11-21): value 9 007 199 254 740 991.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country-level attributes live on `country`), ADR-0002 and ADR-0005
  (public `country.find`, published only, proxy; no change), ADR-0003 (prices never stored),
  ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON; `localeTag` for formatting).
- Revisit when: editors publish inconsistent tables more than occasionally (move to option C with
  a server-side consistency check, or to option A); a country needs a rule input other than age
  and vehicle age; plans need different sensitivities (option D); or a real rating engine replaces
  the simulation.
